title: Elderberry tincture
subtitle: A 1:5 tincture of dried Sambucus nigra berry for immune support during seasonal illness
excerpt: Elderberry tincture is a 1:5 extract of dried, fully ripe Sambucus nigra berries in 25% spirit, taken for 5 to 7 days at the onset of a cold or seasonal flu-like illness. The flavonoid-rich extract has a long tradition in European home herbal practice and has attracted clinical interest for reducing the duration of upper respiratory tract infections. A 100 ml bottle holds about 20 doses. Keeps two years.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), elder entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Sambucus nigra L., fructus (2018, EMA/HMPC/44479/2018), open access. Hawkins J et al., Black elderberry (Sambucus nigra) supplementation is associated with reduced duration of upper respiratory symptoms: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials, Complementary Medicine Research (2019).

glossaryTerms.definition: A large group of plant compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Elderberry is particularly rich in anthocyanins, dark-pigmented flavonoids, that are associated with the berry's reputation for supporting immune defence during viral upper respiratory infections.

content.text: Elderberry herbal extract is a 1:5 extract of dried, fully ripe Sambucus nigra berries in 25% spirit, deep purple-black in colour and sharp-sweet in taste. A long-established European home remedy for the onset of colds and seasonal flu-like illness. The berries are rich in

, particularly anthocyanins, which have attracted genuine clinical interest in recent years. A 2019 meta-analysis found elderberry supplementation reduced the duration of upper respiratory tract infections. Taken for 5 to 7 days at the first sign of illness.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: 25% ABV spirit, mix 1 part 40% vodka with 1 part water to approximate 25%

content.text: Weigh 40 g of dried elderberries into a clean steeping jar. Pour 200 ml of 25% spirit over the berries. The berries will absorb some of the liquid, add a little more spirit if needed to ensure they are submerged.
Seal and label with the date. Store in a cool dark place for 4 to 6 weeks, shaking every few days. The liquid will turn a deep purple-black.
Strain through doubled muslin into a dark glass bottle, pressing the berries thoroughly. Label and store in a cool dark cupboard.

5 ml in a small glass of water, three to four times daily for the first 5 days of a cold or flu-like illness. For immune support at the start of the cold season or before travel, 5 ml once daily for up to 2 weeks.
Sealed dark glass bottle in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the date of straining.
When not to use this remedy

See a doctor for a severe or rapidly worsening illness, high fever above 39 °C, chest symptoms, or any illness that is not clearly a seasonal cold. Elderberry is supportive during mild viral illness. it is not a treatment for serious infection.
